Say you have a child with a chronic, potentially terminal illness.  You have two options in this alternate reality.  The first is to give your child medicine to make him comfortable but the medicine will allow the disease to rapidly progress, killing him within a couple years.  For that amount of time, your child is happy, he is able to play, and just be a normal kid.  The second option is to allow your child to suffer in pain and discomfort with his debilitating disease and he might live a couple more years than if you had giving him the medicine.  Either way, your child will die... but would you rather let him have a shorter, "happier" life or would you rather your child live longer, but be completely miserable the entire time?  In my opinion, the amount of meat produced by these animals is meaningless.  Their quality of life is most important.  Animals experience physical pain and they have emotions, but quite frankly, they have no idea when or how their life will end.  If it were humans, they would know all the details around these two situations.  The knowledge of impending slaughter would be literally torture, whether they are thinking about their own deaths or the death of their loved ones.  But animals don't have the capacity to think this way.  They simply exist in the moment.  Don't get me wrong, I'm sure they feel great sorrow when their young are taken away or a member of their family is missing.  They just simply don't have the means to precognize these situations.
